findings.title: Equal-priority crypto providers are chosen nondeterministically
findings.body: detectProvider now sorts CryptoProvider implementations by order() and always returns the first entry, only debug-logging the rest. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return the same order (200), and Stream.sorted is only stable with respect to ServiceLoader iteration order, which is classpath-dependent. Previously more than one provider on the classpath was a hard failure. A deployment that accidentally has both the default and FIPS (or Elytron) providers will now start with whichever ServiceLoader yields first, so FIPS mode can silently run non-FIPS algorithms or the reverse, with no error and no warning above debug. Lower-priority providers such as AuthzClientCryptoProvider (order 100) should be ignored, but a tie for the highest order must still fail startup.

findings.title: New order() method breaks existing CryptoProvider implementors
findings.body: order() was added as an abstract interface method with no default. CryptoProvider is a public ServiceLoader SPI. Any out-of-tree or older compiled implementation that is not rebuilt against this change will throw AbstractMethodError as soon as CryptoIntegration.detectProvider calls CryptoProvider::order during startup, and source builds of those providers will fail to compile. A default such as default int order() { return 0; } would keep existing providers loadable while still letting in-repo providers override preference.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider returns the default keystore provider
findings.body: When this provider is the one selected (standalone authz-client, where no order-200 provider is present), getBouncyCastleProvider() returns KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider(), which is the JDK keystore provider (typically SUN), not BouncyCastle. WildFlyElytronProvider returns null for the same method so callers can skip BC registration. Callers that register or look up algorithms on this Provider object will use the wrong JCA provider, so BC-only algorithms and provider-name checks fail or run against SUN instead of failing fast with UnsupportedOperationException like the other unimplemented methods on this class.
